title: Still a Work in Progress
author: pghgirl3
content: It’s a good concept and there are things I really like, but overall there’s just too much still missing. Pros: + Daily side quests are a great way to add new goals and get some easy wins to build momentum. + Short, fantasy themed meditations and affirmations are unique and add immersion. + Feels more like an actual game than many other RPG style productivity apps Cons: - Story doesn’t tie into gameplay in any way - No ability to have a custom day start time, so it’s a struggle to maintain streaks if you’re a night owl who checks in after midnight. - Character are sound effects are always male, even if your avatar is female. - Most importantly, there’s no real point to battling monsters. You collect cards that don’t do anything, and the gold and bone dust that you get has no use. I know more features are planned, but there’s not much motivation if nothing has any sense of purpose. I WANT to love this app. I think the potential is there, and there are already some good features, but there’s still a long way to go before this app will be fully realized.

title: A Guided Meditation with compassion
author: TheBatKat
content: As someone with ADHD, I’ve tried meditating and breathing exercises before, but my mind wanders and I feel like a failure and give up. Here, however, the guided meditation specifically calls out this tendency to wander and empathizes with us: it tells us it’s normal and reminds us to just gently bring our thoughts back to the present… Wait? I didn’t completely fail and have to start over because I started thinking about the noise I heard outside which devolved into me thinking about writing a new fantasy language? Score! I gave this app 4 out of 5 stars because I had trouble tracking down the new player guide and then swapping from the guide, back to the app to try the feature I just read about, then back to the guide for the next step. I definitely think that interactively tutorializing the user would benefit the experience. I also downloaded this last night so I have not used it much yet, but I can’t wait to see how this app develops! What new features might the future hold?

title: Loving the motivation
author: BecomingAmazon
content: As someone living in an ADHD household it can be difficult to stay on task and keep life adventurous. I feel like I’m either in play mode with my family while my tasks pile up around me, or I’m hyper focused on catching up and all fun is turned off and I forget to take care of my mental and physical needs. This adventurous app helps to bring balance between my two worlds and bring them together to work in harmony. It helps to bring the fun back into my daily grind, to the point where I look forward to my tasks and each one becomes a piece of the game. I also appreciate how self care is integrated into the app as part of the narrative. If you’re anything like me I would recommend making Modern Sam a part of your day.

title: Keeps me Accountable
author: Balljammin
content: As someone who struggles with ADHD and anxiety, I find myself always feeling completely overwhelmed with tasks at hand. content: Full disclosure: I am a person who served as a beta tester after I had backed this as a Kickstarter project. The most impressive things about this app for me are the responsiveness of the ModernSam devs / staff and the community that the idea of the app spawned. App features I especially love: having the built in nudges for things like "reflect on your day" and I'm also really enjoying the pre-scripted affirmations (gotta unlock the tent for that). The town quests encourage me to try new ways to take care of myself and enable me to reward "simple" tasks that are (meant to be) easy but that I still find difficult. Bestiary / card collector facet helps me stay motivated in following through on trying the town quests and for tracking completion of my tasks including all the little subtask steps. It's not as simple as "have a cup of tea" for some of us. I would break it down as "locate desired tea or blend and a mug", "load teabag", "load kettle with water", "ACTIVATE kettle so the water actually gets hot this time", etc. because there's definitely times where the "ACTIVATE kettle" step got missed... But also, please know that if the existing style of in-app meditations aren't your thing, including if you have no mental image capacity, the affirmations recordings are more versatile for that situation and give the same category of in-game resources. (This is a consideration which has already been brought to the attention of the team, and as regards so many other aspects, they are aiming to update the app moving forward to better reflect the expressed needs of us end users.) Yes, there's work left to do to make this the best possible app. But with other similar apps, I was discouraged by the barebones interface "it's a glorified to do list" or the "I'm not even gonna download it" of not having friends offline to team up with. The community I have acquired via my involvement with helping ModernSam come into being was worth my Kickstarter pledge, no question.

Or a goal in excess of the goal (eg goal of get a $10k raise but I got a $20k raise). 2 - I like that this is focused on the positive, I assume it’s a conscious choice and I think the right one (given how our psychology works). But it would still be good if there was a way to track detracting things as well, structured in a way that doesn’t add too much focus on the negative. Most things are definitely best to frame in the positive - “eat healthy” is a much more productive thought pattern than “don’t eat junk” - because saying don’t do “x” just adds focus to “x”, but some things are hard to track in the positive or are actually best tracked in the negative. E.g. looking at a “no sugar” goal every day in your list could just make you think of sweets and prompt the bad habit, vs seeing nothing and only having to tick off the days you cheated, or maybe there’s some other method. I also think of things like “cheat days”, something you’re allowed to have and want to track, but aren’t a positive that boosts your scores.

That’s made a massive difference in recovery and how sharp I feel mentally. My mind is crystal clear—no more brain fog, sharper focus, and zero tiredness creeping in. Digestion feels smoother (less bloating after meals, easier handling fats), my skin looks brighter and cleaner, and I just feel genuinely healthier from the inside out—like my whole system got a deep, thorough reset and everything’s flowing optimally. And as a nice bonus that I didn’t even expect: I lost almost 10 pounds during the process - and even after going back to normal eating, 6–7 pounds of that has stayed off without any extra effort. My body just feels leaner and less weighed down long-term. The Lifeline Wellness App made it simple to follow each step of the program without feeling overwhelmed. Having a dedicated Care Partner checking in, guiding me, and answering questions made a huge difference — especially on the tougher days. The structure and support really kept me consistent. If you’re hesitating on a proper GBL cleanse, seriously consider it. The process isn’t always glamorous, but the payoff? Feeling cleaner, lighter, more vibrant, with real measurable wins like better sleep metrics, sustained energy, clearer thinking, and that extra weight drop that stuck around. title: UI/UX - From Streamlined to Cumbersome
author: meporter
content: One of the core promises of the 5-Minute Journal is efficiency. It is designed to help users reflect and journal meaningfully in just five minutes. Recent changes to the user experience seem out of alignment with that purpose. When I first started using the app, I could open it and immediately begin my evening entry. I was prompted with the mood check-in, the highlight of the day, what I learned, and my custom questions—all in a smooth, uninterrupted flow. Now, the process is fragmented: * I must manually select my mood after opening the app. * Then, I have to choose “entry feedback” to access the highlight and learning questions. * Finally, I have to edit the entry again to reach my custom prompts. This multi-step interaction interrupts the flow of journaling and makes the experience feel unnecessarily cumbersome. I believe in the intent of this product. Please consider streamlining the experience again to preserve what made it valuable: simplicity and speed.

title: Good but use with caution.
author: mikeydoeswork
content: Faith Guide does a better job than most faith-based AI tools at respecting Scripture, maintaining a pastoral tone, and avoiding reckless certainty. It quotes the Bible accurately, encourages prayer and counsel, and avoids claiming to speak directly for God; which already puts it ahead of many similar apps. That said, users should be aware of an important limitation. When Scripture does not clearly provide an answer, the guidance quietly shifts toward internal discernment. In practice, this often leads to deferring decisions rather than providing clear biblical boundaries, even in challenging situations that Scripture can meaningfully constrain. Over time, this can place unnecessary psychological and spiritual weight on users, especially when facing high-stakes or emotionally charged decisions. Overall, it’s a thoughtful tool for reflection, but users should be cautious about relying on it alone for complex moral or life-altering choices.

title: Great content, serious interfacing issues
author: courteneylj
content: I’ve had this app for a few months and the idea behind it is great. They have great classes from a variety of teachers. However, the app needs a serious overhaul. Everything about it is not user friendly. Trying to saving classes for future use is a nightmare. They all go to one place and you can’t categorize them. You can only put them in a certain order in one giant list so I’ve created “playlists” in a way but this is the biggest nightmare of them all. It took me about 45 minutes to organize maybe 50 classes so that my yin classes aren’t all intertwined with my strong flow classes. Every time you move a class anywhere in the list, it takes you all the way to the top of list. Then you have to scroll back down to continue organizing. The other frustrating part is the fact that if the class has a long name (like longer than 5 words) there is no way of knowing what it’s called. From the list you can read about 4 words and even after clicking on the class, you can read about 5 and then... this is a huge problem when trying to decide what class to begin. Especially considering every time you click on a class it resets the suggestions and takes you to the top again so you have to commit to a class based on a thumbnail and half the title. It’s really not what I want to deal with when trying to be in a state of peace so I find myself opting not to use the app at all sometimes if I’m anxious or have low patience.. which are exactly the times I’d like to have someone else guide me through a practice... in this day and age and for $20 a month with I’m sure hundreds of thousands of subscribers, you could really stand to pay someone to fix these fundamental problems. The last time I used something so bug ridden was using a motorola droid with nearly the first edition of android operating system running it. I expect more for the price I pay. If the problem is not resolved soon, I’ll look for another service provider or just go back to YouTube where things are simple and free to boot

Sometimes the whole app just won’t load, like today, and when that happens I delete the app and reload it. So remember the email and password you used when you signed up. It actually doesn’t take that long. There’s so much amazing content in this app that all of this is worth it. There are many knowledgeable teachers there are good courses and there are classes of all lengths of time and a wide range of abilities. What I love most about this app and this site is that it is so completely inclusive and has classes for anyone of any age any size and any ability. Other yoga sites and yoga apps portray the yogi In an unrealistic manner and reinforce negative and damaging content and images. It is also important to note that this site/app is not just about Asana. Which if you know anything about yoga, asana is only one limb of eight. title: Lots of potential but…
author: MotherofDragonsFirstofHerName
content: This app is beautiful and it has lots of potential however where it seems to fall short is in the implementation. Directions: there are not clear directions on how all the functions in the app work. You just have to try And see what they do. For instance I didn’t know there was an option to turn off the voice in WBTB until I accidentally pressed it. Subliminals: First the AI voices are horrible. It is possible to have natural sounding AI voices at this point but that’s not what they have. You can record your own voice though but that leads to the second problem which is that there is no way to change the volume on the recording. You also can not review the recording once you save it, you can use it or delete it but not view the affirmations or edit it. The volume of the recording is definitely not at subliminal level. And the ambient audios (rain ocean etc;) only play for 4 minutes. The shifting audios: the audio shouldn’t say CR or DR but rather current reality or desired reality…those terms keep the cadence. The audio and the ambient sound cut out abruptly in the heartbeat method literally mid sentence. It’s weird. It may be because I had it at .75 speed…if so that’s a syncing issue that needs to fixed. I’d also love the option of choosing either a female voice or a male voice for each method. WBTB: This feature is the reason I paid for the app, as I saw an ad that mentioned it. Again no directions so you know what to expect. No way to choose the alarm sound or volume, or information to know what the sound or volume are. The first night I thought I’d set the alarm and I hadn’t. The next night I set the alarm correctly but at the default setting so it didn’t go off at the right time. The third night the alarm went off but was too low for me to hear it (and I’m a light sleeper). I’ll try again but this is an advertised feature and it seems like more work needs to be placed into it. I believe this app will be phenomenal once all the features work

title: NOT a ‘free’ trial - User beware
author: alexandramonet
content: I downloaded this app out of sheer curiosity for the name and some of the images posted on the promotion page in the App Store. I have been studying mythology and iconography for my own research and interest on the topic and while I can’t state the accuracy of the information, it seems well designed. The videos are not presented by native English speakers, which is fine, but sometimes the information can seem biased and culturally based, rather than universal concepts. Thus, upon sign up, I was going through the app a bit and received a pop up to try the membership titled “Try for Free” (verbatim). I put in my email and information and found out later that I was charged immediately after signing up for the free trial. It seems very dishonest, and instead of enjoying and experimenting with the app to see if I might want to maintain a membership after the free period, I now won’t continue supporting the company because I don’t appreciate being deceived. Whether it is a programming error or a deceptive intentional sales tactic on behalf of the founder and company, I certainly won’t be returning for this subscription. I have read a few other reviews sharing a similar experience with the “free” not free trial, so just stay aware and be attentive to what you are signing up for, as it is misleading. I’ve reached out to customer support (like many others) and have not yet received a response. All my best for the improvement of service, I hope changes may come soon or this app will likely not succeed.

author: Fizacleezy
content: I’ll start off saying I really like this app! The User Interface is easy and smooth! The AI chat function is awesome and Coach John is by far my favorite! content: oh my god don’t look at my screen name 🫣 i’m not a fan of ai, in fact i actively abstain. this, however, seemingly uses technology i’ve utilized for years. something akin to google lense, then past that it just follows what they’ve plugged in to it for analysis and how to speak about food (sans shame, diet culture, and pseudoscience. something i feel like i have to personally fistfight god to achieve in my reception of online content) the only thing that leans in to the (typically rancid) AI feel is the cute names it gives your dishes, calling my spicy creamy ramen concoction “spicy american ramen”, which i don’t actually mind. its not drowning in ads, it has minimal fluff, very straightforward, and the recommendations so far (suggesting greek yogurt or nuts with my snack of rice cakes and a banana) are EXACTLY what i think we should be doing when speaking about nutrition. that is meaningful impact made accessible. do not skip the three slides after submitting your photos (i almost have multiple times). i’ll definitely be using this daily just the way that it is.

title: Great start- improvement’s needed
author: Ms. Jo 2U
content: I love everything Zoe is about- except for the foods database in the app. The foods database is lacking; it’s lacking nutrition info for major foods/major food chains in my area, and it’s tedious and frustrating to scroll and scroll for ingredients that are something somewhat similar to what I’m eating, and even more tedious to enter items for review. I don’t necessarily use the same ingredients for the items I make (eg my salad isn’t always the same) however, most of the ingredients of my salad are. I believe that purchasing organic and regenerative items makes a tremendous difference in my health, but the app rarely has those ingredients. The feature that takes a picture and analyzes the food is mind-blowingly phenomenal, however, for me-is unhelpful if all of the food are based on foods I don’t eat. The app doesn’t remember or incorporate the ingredients I scan, so I either have to have all of the original packaging (I meal prep for the week and don’t have the packaging with me), select what their database has, or not bother. Once they finally update the food database- I think the app will be great. For me, for now- it’s just too tedious to track food with. The food chain databases I’d like added (in the US) are Trader Joe’s, Whole Foods, Safeway, Key Food, Stop & Shop, and Wegmans.

title: Helped with aches & pains!
author: Walkerc56789
content: I’ve been using the Zoe AI Meal Tracker with no subscription for 276 days. Initially in the first few months, I dropped 7 pounds without even trying. With ongoing use, I’ve noticed my worst aches & pains have subsided greatly. An orthopedic surgeon told me both shoulders should be replaced, but the pain I had is mostly gone. Even after doing rigorous gardening last summer that would ordinarily result in lots of pain. Choosing mindfully has definitely helped my arthritis/inflammation. Using the scanner is very helpful in allowing me to choose better options at the grocery store. I found a bread (Hero) that scores 100. Scanning different varieties of granola, I’ve discovered that a grain free one might score 80-90, while those with grains only get 40-50. I aim to choose items 70 points & above. I do like to snack & most sweet or salty snacks don’t get high scores, but have found some around 60 points & some higher 80-90 like seedz crackers & these can satisfy a craving. Frozen cherries are a nice icy snack at 100 points. Some of the things I used to eat regularly, are now eliminated entirely. I just don’t want to eat something that scores 0-30 & rarely purchase those anymore. I’ve found the app to be mostly accurate, but it can misidentify some photographed items. Salmon has frequently been identified as chicken, particularly if there’s a topping of some sort. Initially, my app gave an Aperol spritz 100 points, which I knew couldn’t be the case. I notified Zoe & it’s been updated. I was considering a subscription, but see many reviews with low ratings for that, so I’m sticking with my free Zoe

title: Potential to be an incredible tool
author: Herbertween
content: This app is absolutely incredible in theory. The first couple weeks I used it I was blown away at how much better than my actual therapist it seemed to be. It not being a real person actually helps in some ways because I’m much less worried about judgement and feel more open. Also the frequency I can journal puts this way ahead of my guy I saw once a week. However… there are two issues I have with this app in its current state. One significant issue and one annoyance. Annoyance: the voice transcription feature is great because it feels much more natural to get thoughts out at the speed of talking. However, the “immersion” is immediately broken when you then have to wait for it to transcribe… then submit it… then wait for the response tokens to come in… then wait for the voice model to start reading it. If there was a way to get it closer to the voice experience one has with something like ChatGPT where it feels more conversational I think that would go a long way. Significant Issue: the models that are being used in the background are not smart enough. At times they are great if your topics are straightforward. However if there is even the slightest bit of complexity in a timeline of events you have or you dare talk about two topics in a single entry it will crumble. It has no logic at all and often combines events from different stories like my grandmother used to in the later stages of her dementia. This is within a single entry too… this isn’t when it’s remembering events from past entries. And when you are building an app for something as intimate as Rosebud… as soon as the model doesn’t appear to be listening or comes across like an idiot it completely ruins what should be a healing experience. The voice feature would be cool but the latter is the real thing that will prevent me from renewing a subscription. If you could please please please use smarter models this app would actually be life changing.

title: Fantastic!

content: This app is so wonderful, genuinely. The team behind the app is so kind, as well. I’ve had to reach out to them and Bjorn is lovely. If you’re looking for a great meditation app, this one should be on your list. One of the best things about this app, for me, is that most of the singles tailored to your mood are short and able to be done in public, at work, whatever. A lot of them involve keeping your eyes open, and noticing the world around you, which is great when you’re out and about. The courses are wonderful, and the self-care one specifically is great for connecting with your emotions. The breathing section is also extremely helpful, especially when it’s an SOS type situation. The Focus tab is helpful, as it allows you to set it up so that picking up your phone will ruin your focus session. Aside from that, the way the app tracks your progress is unique. Instead of simply telling you how many sessions you’ve done or how many minutes you’ve meditated, the app does this AND you start to grow a tree within the app. Each session grows your tree, and I love that. It gives a small connection to nature, although digital, and it’s such a cute idea. The price is really fair, especially since most meditation apps are around double the monthly price. To the MindFi team, thank you for creating such a useful and beautiful meditation app. I’m excited to see what you all keep doing! (Ps. More courses and moods are an exciting idea 😉).
